headline: Protein language model embeddings are repurposed for PTM and functional prediction
label: Protein Language Model Applications
summary: Pretrained protein and RNA language model embeddings are being benchmarked and repurposed for modification, function, and binding-site prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of pretrained sequence language model representations for site- and function-level prediction. The arXiv benchmark evaluates 13 protein language models across 15 downstream tasks and 9 datasets, finding intermediate layers often beat last-layer embeddings. Several preprints apply embeddings to PTM site prediction: an anchor-guided rectified flow matching framework covers six PTMs, and the published CLASPP model predicts multiple PTM types per site. FuncSeek fuses ESM2, ProstT5 and ProteinBERT embeddings via supervised contrastive learning for EC-based functional similarity search. RNA preprints apply the same logic to nucleotide sequence, including PARNET, SPIRAL on BiRNA-BERT, and TriTower-m6Am. The new element is layer-level selection and interpretability alongside end-task accuracy.
